subject: social
name: Social Studies
course: United States History: Revolution through Reconstruction (1754–1877)
title: Grade 8 Social Studies: United States History: Revolution through Reconstruction (1754–1877)
overview: Grade 8 Social Studies engages students in historical inquiry, primary source analysis, geographic mapping, and civic deliberation aligned with the C3 Framework.
competencies: Corroborate primary documents with historical context and point-of-view analysis.
Explain how geographical trade networks and physical barriers shaped civilizations.
Analyze economic developments, resource allocation, and market exchanges.
Assess the evolution of democratic values, civil liberties, and civic responsibilities.

modules.title: The Road to Revolution & the Birth of the Republic (1754–1789)
modules.description: Analyzing the French and Indian War, colonial protest, the Declaration of Independence, the Revolutionary War, and the Constitution.

topics.title: Colonial Grievances and the War for Independence
topics.description: Investigating taxation policies, the Boston Massacre, Common Sense, and military turning points at Saratoga and Yorktown.

topics.title: The Constitutional Convention and the Bill of Rights
topics.description: Analyzing the Great Compromise, the Federalist vs. Anti-Federalist debates, separation of powers, and the Bill of Rights.

modules.title: Westward Expansion, Jacksonian Democracy & Sectionalism (1800–1860)
modules.description: Exploring the Louisiana Purchase, Indian Removal, Manifest Destiny, Northern industrialization, and the Southern cotton kingdom.

topics.title: The Louisiana Purchase and Manifest Destiny
topics.description: Tracing the Lewis and Clark expedition, the Mexican-American War, and the California Gold Rush.

topics.title: Jacksonian Politics and the Trail of Tears
topics.description: Examining expanded suffrage for white males, bank wars, and the forced expulsion of Cherokee and Creek nations.

topics.title: Sectionalism and the Moral Struggle Over Slavery
topics.description: Contrasting the abolitionist movement (Douglass, Tubman), the Underground Railroad, and the Missouri Compromise.

modules.title: The Civil War & the Reconstruction Era (1861–1877)
modules.description: Analyzing secession, turning point battles of the Civil War, the Emancipation Proclamation, and the Reconstruction Amendments.

topics.title: The American Civil War: Strategy, Battlefields and Emancipation
topics.description: Analyzing Fort Sumter, Antietam, Gettysburg, Lincoln's Gettysburg Address, and the military collapse of the Confederacy.

topics.title: Reconstruction: The 13th, 14th, and 15th Amendments and Backlash
topics.description: Examining Black political leadership in the South, the rise of the Ku Klux Klan, sharecropping, and the Compromise of 1877.
